skill.name: neon-postgres
skill.description: Guides and best practices for working with Lakebase Postgres, the database behind Neon. Covers setup, connection methods and drivers, pooled vs direct connections, branching, schema migrations, autoscaling, scale-to-zero, instant restore, read replicas, connection pooling, IP allow lists, and logical replication. Use when users ask about "Lakebase Postgres", "Neon setup", "connect to Neon", "Neon project", "DATABASE_URL", "serverless Postgres", "Neon CLI", "neon", "Neon MCP", "Neon Auth", "@neondatabase/serverless", "@neondatabase/neon-js", "scale to zero", "Neon autoscaling", "Neon read replica", "Neon connection pooling", or "schema migrations".
skill.summary: Plan and operate Neon Postgres connections, branches, migrations, scaling, recovery, replicas, pooling, access controls, and replication.
skill.author: neondatabase

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, variable names, and links to official Neon documentation. Confirmed risks are unpinned remote skill installation and CLI-driven database credential handling; no prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends fetching or installing additional skills from mutable remote sources.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation, pin a reviewed commit or release, and inspect downloaded instructions before loading them.

remediation.issue: The setup flow retrieves database credentials and writes them to a local environment file.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the destination, preserve existing values, require restrictive permissions, verify git exclusion, and never print the connection string.

content.value_statement: Neon projects require careful choices for connections, migrations, scaling, and recovery. This skill provides focused guidance for dependable Postgres workflows on Neon.
actual_capabilities: Guides Neon organization, project, and connection setup.
Explains pooled and direct connection selection by workload.
Recommends drivers for Vercel, Cloudflare, Neon Functions, and edge runtimes.
Guides branch-based migration testing and schema management.
Explains autoscaling, scale-to-zero, restore, and read replica behavior.
Covers IP allow lists, connection pooling, and logical replication.
limitations: Requires Neon CLI, MCP, or console access for live project operations.
Does not replace application-specific ORM or migration documentation.
Does not guarantee plan availability, limits, or current pricing.
Handles connection guidance but does not audit database schemas or queries.

use_cases.title: Configure a Serverless Application
use_cases.description: Select a compatible driver and pooled connection strategy for a deployed application.

use_cases.title: Test a Production Migration
use_cases.description: Create an isolated branch and plan migration testing with a direct connection.

use_cases.title: Plan Database Operations
use_cases.description: Evaluate scaling, recovery, replicas, access controls, and replication for production requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me connect [application] on [runtime] to Neon. Recommend the driver and pooled or direct connection, then explain the choice.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a safe [ORM] schema migration for my Neon project. Include branch testing, connection type, validation, and production rollout steps.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Scaling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this workload profile: [details]. Recommend Neon autoscaling, scale-to-zero, pooling, and read replica settings with trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Neon Postgres architecture for [system]. Cover branching, migrations, recovery, access controls, pooling, replicas, and logical replication.

output_examples.input: Which connection should a serverless web application use?
output_examples.output: Use the pooled connection for normal application queries. Keep the direct connection available for migrations and session-dependent operations.

output_examples.input: How should I test a schema migration before production?
output: Create a branch from production data.
Run the migration through a direct connection.
Validate application behavior and rollback procedures.
Apply the reviewed migration to production.

output_examples.input: Can read replicas reduce primary read load?
output_examples.output: Yes. Neon read replicas provide independent read-only compute while sharing storage with the primary branch.

best_practices: Use pooled connections for application traffic and direct connections for migrations, dumps, and replication.
Test schema changes on a production branch before applying them to production.
Store connection strings securely and exclude environment files from version control.
anti_patterns: Do not run migration tools through a pooled transaction-mode connection.
Do not mix manual schema changes with ORM-managed migration history.
Do not place database connection strings in prompts, logs, or source control.

faq.question: Does this skill create Neon projects?
faq.answer: It guides project selection and creation through Neon CLI or MCP when those tools are available.

faq.question: Which connection should web applications use?
faq.answer: Most web and serverless applications should use the pooled connection for normal query traffic.

faq.question: Which connection should migrations use?
faq.answer: Migrations should use the direct connection because transaction pooling does not preserve required session behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill support Neon branches?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains branch use cases and directs detailed branch creation to the related branch skill.

faq.question: Can it recommend a database driver?
faq.answer: Yes. Recommendations cover node-postgres, Neon serverless drivers, and several deployment runtimes.

faq.question: Does it manage credentials safely?
faq.answer: It recommends local environment storage, but users must control permissions, version control exclusions, and secret handling.
